1: # DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)
2: 
3: Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
4: PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
5: messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
6: ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
7: Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
8: thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).
9: 
10: ## Conventions
11: - Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
12:   prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
13:   `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
14:   now()`, `updated_at`.
15: - All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
16:   or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
17: - RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
18:   (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
19: - text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.
20: 
21: ## Tables
22: 
23: ### 1. `workspaces`
24: | col | type | notes |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | id | text pk | `wp_` prefix |
27: | name | text not null | e.g. "Personal" |
28: | created_by | uuid not null ref auth.users | |
29: | is_default | bool not null default false | PERSONAL per-user |
30: | created_at / updated_at | | |
31: Index: `(created_by, name)` unique.
32: RLS: owner only.
33: > MVP: auto-created "Personal" per user (is_default). Users can ALSO be added
34: > as members to OTHER workspaces via workspace invites — those workspaces show
35: > in the switcher (badge if not owner). Creating extra own-workspaces is a
36: > pro/future feature (plan limits: free = 1 owned, 3 groups, 5 threads/group).
37: 
38: ### 2. `groups`  ← sidebar folder of threads (the "group" concept)
39: | col | type | notes |
40: |---|---|---|
41: | id | text pk `grp_` |
42: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
43: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator |
44: | name | text not null | PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES, user-created groups… |
45: | kind | enum(custom, system) default custom | system = PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES |
46: | position | int default 0 |
47: | created_at / updated_at |
48: Unique (workspace_id, name). Indexes: (workspace_id, position).
49: RLS: owner OR member. Readable to user when owner or workspace member.
50: > **INVITES is a REAL system group** created at signup (with PERSONAL, SITE,
51: > WORKFLOWS). It is LOCKED: cannot be renamed/deleted, user cannot manually add
52: > a thread to it. It only gets populated when the user ACCEPTS a thread invite;
53: > then the owner's thread appears there. Guest cannot add anything to INVITES
54: > unless invited.
55: 
56: ### 3. `workspace_members`  ← who is in the workspace (owner/editor/viewer)
57: | col | type | notes |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | id | text pk `wme_` |
60: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces on delete cascade |
61: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users |
62: | role | enum(owner, editor, viewer) default viewer |
63: | created_at |
64: Unique (workspace_id, user_id). Creator auto-inserted as `owner` by trigger.
65: RLS: owner manages (CUD); members SELECT.
66: > Joined workspace = access to the OWNER's real workspace (all groups + threads
67: > visible to every member). Roles: owner=full, editor=work (create/edit/run/
68: > delete any thread/group, edit plans), viewer=read-only. NO owner/admin/member.
69: 
70: ### 4. `user_profiles`
71: | col | type | notes |
72: |---|---|---|
73: | id | text pk `prf_` |
74: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users unique |
75: | onboarded | bool default false |
76: | pre_answers | jsonb | signup question answers (JSON-driven onboarding) |
77: | plan | enum(free, pro) default free |
78: | prefer_own_keys_in_shared | bool default false | profile toggle: "use my own key in invited workspaces" |
79: | created_at / updated_at |
80: RLS: `auth.uid()`. Written at signup, editable in Profile dialog.
81: 
82: ### 5. `threads`  ← chat container AND (bound) workflow
83: | col | type | notes |
84: |---|---|---|
85: | id | text pk `thd_` |
86: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
87: | group_id | text ref groups null | which sidebar group it lives in |
88: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator/owner |
89: | title | text not null default '' | auto-titled from 1st user message (smart title); rename in header input still available |
90: | deleted_at | timestamptz null | soft-archive: null = live; set on delete → recoverable 30 days, then hard-delete |

92: | bound_workflow_id | text ref workflows null | set by LLM `finalizeAndInject` tool |
93: | created_at / updated_at / last_message_at |
94: Indexes: (user_id, workspace_id, last_message_at desc); (group_id);
95: trigram or lower(title) for search.
96: RLS: owner OR workspace member OR via `thread_shares` (invitee sees it in
97: their own sidebar's INVITES system group).
98: > Thread identifies chat AND workflow (1:1). Must have at least null wf until bound.
99: > Limits: ≤5 threads per group, ≤3 groups per workspace (free plan) — enforced
100: > at insert (RPC / service), counted per workspace.
101: 
102: ### 6. `workflows`
103: | col | type | notes |
104: |---|---|---|
105: | id | text pk `wf_` |
106: | thread_id | text ref threads null | bind target (nullable pre-bind) |

119: `plans`: id `pln_`, workflow_id (unique), title, objective, summary, status
120: enum(draft, proposed, accepted, declined), created_at, updated_at.
121: `plan_steps`: id `pls_`, plan_id ref cascade, position int, title, description,

126: | col | type | notes |
127: |---|---|---|
128: | id | text pk `msg_` |
129: | thread_id | text ref threads cascade |

260: | id | text pk `fil_` |
261: | user_id | uuid |
262: | thread_id | text ref threads null |
263: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
264: | bucket | text default 'chat-attachments' |
265: | path | text not null | storage path `{user}/{thread}/{ulid}.ext` |
266: | mime_type | text |
267: | size_bytes | bigint |
268: | compressed | bool default false |
269: | created_at |
270: RLS: owner. Storage bucket policy: authenticate (owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}/`).
271: 
272: ### 17. `notification_webhooks` (optional future) — REMOVED from MVP, note only.
273: External webhooks folded into `notifications` + Inngest `notification/publish`,
274: existing `webhook-board`/`waitForWebhook` retired.
275: 
276: ## Enums (Postgres)
277: ```
278: role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
279: thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
280: plan            : free|pro
281: group_kind      : custom|system
282: invite_kind     : workspace|thread
283: invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
284: workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
285: message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
286: message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
287: run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
288: activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
289: activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
290: approval_status : pending|approved|denied
291: api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
292: ```
293: 
294: ## Supabase specifics
295: - Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
296: - **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
297:   `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
298: - **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
299:   dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
300:   CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
301: - **RLS policy list**:
302:   - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
303:     files (+ own invites).
304:   - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
305:     chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
306:     OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
307:   - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
308:     `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
309:     group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
310:   - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
311:     `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
312:     workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
313:     exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
314:     → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
315: - **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
316:   `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
317:   `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
318:   (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.
319: 
320: ## Why this shape (reasoning)
321: - `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
322:   sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
323: - `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
324:   custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
325:   until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
326:   ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
327: - `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
328:   accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
329: - `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
330:   run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
331:   `threads.user_id`).
332: - `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
333:   replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
334: - `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
335:   directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
336:   killing the god-table smell.
337: - `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
338:   by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
339: - Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
340:   → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

<content>
1: # ENV — Variables & User-Suppliable Keys
2: 
3: Three layers: **server/infra env** (Vercel/Next server, never client),
4: **user workspace keys** (entered by user in Workflow Settings → Agent/Env tab,
5: stored in DB, encrypted), and **per-thread overrides** (rare, optional).
6: 
7: ## Existing env (old backend → what to keep)
8: 
9: | Var | Used by (old) | New use |
10: |---|---|---|
11: | `DATABASE_URL` / `DIRECT_URL` | drizzle pg | → Supabase project connection string (keep, used by drizzle) |
12: | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` / `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | better-auth | **DELETE** (Supabase Auth owns sessions) |
13: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | unused today | keep — supabase-js client |
14: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | unused today | keep — anon role for RLS/DATA API |
15: | `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | — | **ADD** server-only, storage uploads + admin (never NEXT_PUBLIC) |
16: | `ANAKIN_API_KEY` / `ANAKIN_BASE_URL` | agent adapters | fallback default; user can override per workspace |
17: | `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` | runtime | fallback defaults; per workspace override |
18: | `MEM0_API_KEY` | workflow mem0 | fallback; per workspace override |
19: | `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` / `SIGNING_KEY` / `APP_ID` | inngest client | keep |
20: | `WEBHOOK_BASE_URL` | webhook-board | keep |
21: | `AGENT_MAX_STEPS` / `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` / `RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | inngest | keep as server caps (hard ceiling) |
22: 
23: ## NEW env (definitive list, final)
24: 
25: ```
26: # --- Supabase ---
27: DATABASE_URL                # postgres connection for drizzle (direct)
28: DIRECT_URL                  # pooler direct url (non-pooled, for migrations)
29: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL    # client
30: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY  # client anon (never secret)
31: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   # server only — storage bucket mgmt, user creation
32: SUPABASE_AUTH_SECRET        # optional: for verifying webhook JWT from auth hooks
33: 
34: # --- Inngest ---
35: INNGEST_EVENT_KEY
36: INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY
37: INNGEST_APP_ID
38: 
39: # --- Webhook interop ---
40: WEBHOOK_BASE_URL            # base url for generated /api/v1/hooks/:token urls
41: 
42: # --- Defaults (single fallback key each; user overrides per-workspace in UI) ---
43: ANAKIN_API_KEY
44: ANAKIN_BASE_URL             # default https://api.anakin.io/v1
45: GROQ_API_KEY
46: GROQ_MODEL                  # default text model, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-20b
47: MEM0_API_KEY
48: 
49: # --- Server hard caps (clamp user values; not editable by user) ---
50: AGENT_MAX_STEPS             # default 5      — ceiling
51: AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS        # default 50     — ceiling
52: EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS       # default 900    — ceiling
53: EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD      # default 1      — ceiling
54: EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS # default 604800 — ceiling
55: RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS       # default 2      — ceiling
56: 
57: # --- Model routing (per category; fall back from workspace → env default) ---
58: TEXT_MODEL                   # alias of GROQ_MODEL default (kept by name parity)
59: IMAGE_MODEL                  # default e.g. groq/text2img or provider, optional
60: SPEECH_MODEL                 # optional
61: TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL          # optional
62: VIDEO_MODEL                  # optional (future)
63: ```
64: 
65: > Client (`packages/env/src/web.ts`) must expose only:
66: > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
67: > Everything else stays server-only. `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION` respected.
68: 
69: ## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)
70: 
71: Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
72: "Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:
73: 
74: - Groq API key + Groq model (text)
75: - Anakin API key + base URL
76: - Mem0 API key
77: - (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides
78: 
79: Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
80: `workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.
81: 
82: Resolution order at call time:
83: ```
84: 1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
85:      → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
86: 2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
87: 3. env default
88: ```
89: `workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way (rare).
90: Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
91: Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
92: **Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.
93: 
94: > Note: ChatComposer token slider = "max tokens per chat request" — maps to
95: > `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, NOT a run budget. Server caps
96: > (`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` etc.) remain hard ceilings.
97: 
98: ## Best placement reasoning
99: - Workspace is the right scope: keys belong to a workspace, reusable in the
100:   `PERSONAL` workspace and future ones. Thread-level is pointless UX (user
101:   shouldn't re-enter per thread); we allow per-thread override but never require.
102: - Server retains hard caps so a user cannot self-grant unlimited budgets.
103: - Never ship keys to client — tools run server-side (Inngest/route), so only
104:   server reads them.

(End of file - total 104 lines)
</content>

65: ## 3. Confirmed breakages (behind "cron not working", "AI SDK not working")

67: 1. **`schedule-tick` has no trigger and is never served.**

69:    `inngest.createFunction({ id: "schedule-tick", retries: 2 }, ...)` with no
70:    `triggers` array, and `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts:9` registers
71:    ONLY `executionRun`. Result: cron jobs, sleep→wake, and due-work sweeping
72:    can never fire. This is the root cause of "cron broken".
73: 
74: 2. **`notificationNotifier` is also never served.** `notification/publish`
75:    events (`execution-run.ts:763`) are dropped at the SDK boundary → webhook
76:    notifications and anywhere-outside-the-app delivery are dead.

78: 3. **`resumeWorkflow` does nothing useful.**
79:    `workflow-service.ts:1024` flips `paused → active` but never enqueues a new
80:    execution or sends `execution/run`. A "resumed" workflow sits idle forever.
81: 
82: 4. **Orphaned executions on event-send failure.** Every mutator in
83:    `agent.ts` (`sendMessage`, `confirmWorkflow`, `updateObjective`,
84:    `runWorkflow`, `resolveApproval`) follows
85:    `enqueueMessage() → inngest.send()` and on send error calls
86:    `failExecution()`, but the row created by `enqueueMessage` stays
87:    `pending`. If `inngest.send` throws after enqueue, nothing ever processes
88:    that execution → permanent orphan. This send+fail block is copy-pasted 5×
89:    and is the prime candidate to kill when `/api/chat` takes over.

98:    `result.usage.costUsd > EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` AFTER the whole run completes
99:    (`execution-run.ts:594`). It can never stop a run from overspending, it only
100:    schedules a recovery afterwards.
101: 
102: 7. **`replayedToolOutputs` is keyed by tool name** (`runtime.ts:160`) and
103:    consumed once. Fine for the single-retry case, but two capabilities with the
104:    same name would collide; also replay happens before the response cap, so a
105:    huge persisted output can refill context.

108:    Verify this exact model id exists on Groq — if the dev was running a local
109:    override this default may 404 in production. `MEM0_API_KEY` defaults to `""`
110:    (silent no-op backend).

1: # DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)
2: 
3: Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
4: PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
5: messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
6: ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
7: Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
8: thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).
9: 
10: ## Conventions
11: - Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
12:   prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
13:   `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
14:   now()`, `updated_at`.
15: - All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
16:   or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
17: - RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
18:   (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
19: - text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.
20: 
21: ## Tables
22: 
23: ### 1. `workspaces`
24: | col | type | notes |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | id | text pk | `wp_` prefix |
27: | name | text not null | e.g. "Personal" |
28: | created_by | uuid not null ref auth.users | |
29: | is_default | bool not null default false | PERSONAL per-user |
30: | created_at / updated_at | | |
31: Index: `(created_by, name)` unique.
32: RLS: owner only.
33: > MVP: auto-created "Personal" per user (is_default). Users can ALSO be added
34: > as members to OTHER workspaces via workspace invites — those workspaces show
35: > in the switcher (badge if not owner). Creating extra own-workspaces is a
36: > pro/future feature (plan limits: free = 1 owned, 3 groups, 5 threads/group).
37: 
38: ### 2. `groups`  ← sidebar folder of threads (the "group" concept)
39: | col | type | notes |
40: |---|---|---|
41: | id | text pk `grp_` |
42: | workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
43: | user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator |
44: | name | text not null | PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES, user-created groups… |
45: | kind | enum(custom, system) default custom | system = PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES |
46: | position | int default 0 |
47: | created_at / updated_at |

285: message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
286: message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
287: run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled

289: activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system

292: ```
293: 
294: ## Supabase specifics
295: - Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
296: - **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
297:   `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
298: - **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
299:   dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
300:   CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
301: - **RLS policy list**:
302:   - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
303:     files (+ own invites).
304:   - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
305:     chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
306:     OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
307:   - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
308:     `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
309:     group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
310:   - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
311:     `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
312:     workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
313:     exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
314:     → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
315: - **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
316:   `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
317:   `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
318:   (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.
319: 
320: ## Why this shape (reasoning)
321: - `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
322:   sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
323: - `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
324:   custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
325:   until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
326:   ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
327: - `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
328:   accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
329: - `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
330:   run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
331:   `threads.user_id`).
332: - `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
333:   replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
334: - `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
335:   directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
336:   killing the god-table smell.
337: - `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
338:   by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
339: - Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
340:   → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

**Confirmed in your drizzle-orm 0.45.2:**
- `pgPolicy()` + `.enableRLS()` on every table ✅

**NOT possible in drizzle (no API in 0.45.2):**
- Triggers (`pgTrigger` is still an unmerged PR) → `on_auth_user_created`, limits triggers
- Realtime publications, storage bucket + policies

**1. Delete** `20260911120000_new_schema.sql` (all 3 of its DDL blocks are now in generated `0001`).

SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   # server only — storage bucket mgmt, user creation
SUPABASE_AUTH_SECRET        # optional: for verifying webhook JWT from auth hooks

# --- Inngest ---
INNGEST_EVENT_KEY
INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY
INNGEST_APP_ID

# --- Webhook interop ---
WEBHOOK_BASE_URL            # base url for generated /api/v1/hooks/:token urls

# --- Defaults (single fallback key each; user overrides per-workspace in UI) ---
ANAKIN_API_KEY
ANAKIN_BASE_URL             # default https://api.anakin.io/v1
GROQ_API_KEY
GROQ_MODEL                  # default text model, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-20b
MEM0_API_KEY

# --- Server hard caps (clamp user values; not editable by user) ---
AGENT_MAX_STEPS             # default 5      — ceiling
AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS        # default 50     — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS       # default 900    — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD      # default 1      — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS # default 604800 — ceiling
RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS       # default 2      — ceiling

# --- Model routing (per category; fall back from workspace → env default) ---
TEXT_MODEL                   # alias of GROQ_MODEL default (kept by name parity)
IMAGE_MODEL                  # default e.g. groq/text2img or provider, optional
SPEECH_MODEL                 # optional
TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL          # optional
VIDEO_MODEL                  # optional (future)
```

> Client (`packages/env/src/web.ts`) must expose only:
> `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
> Everything else stays server-only. `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION` respected.

## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)

Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
"Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:

- Groq API key + Groq model (text)
- Anakin API key + base URL
- Mem0 API key
- (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides

Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
`workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.

Resolution order at call time:
```
1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
     → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env default
```
`workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way (rare).
Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
**Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.

> Note: ChatComposer token slider = "max tokens per chat request" — maps to
> `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, NOT a run budget. Server caps
> (`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` etc.) remain hard ceilings.

## Best placement reasoning
- Workspace is the right scope: keys belong to a workspace, reusable in the
  `PERSONAL` workspace and future ones. Thread-level is pointless UX (user
  shouldn't re-enter per thread); we allow per-thread override but never require.
- Server retains hard caps so a user cannot self-grant unlimited budgets.
- Never ship keys to client — tools run server-side (Inngest/route), so only
  server reads them.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

13: ## Proxy
14: 
15: > **Good to know**: Starting with Next.js 16, Middleware is now called Proxy to better reflect its purpose. The functionality remains the same.
16: 
17: Proxy allows you to run code before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.
18: 
19: ### Use cases
20: 
21: Some common scenarios where Proxy is effective include:
22: 
23: - Modifying headers for all pages or a subset of pages
24: - Rewriting to different pages based on A/B tests or experiments
25: - Programmatic redirects based on incoming request properties
26: 
27: For simple redirects, consider using the [`redirects`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/redirects) configuration in `next.config.ts` first. Proxy should be used when you need access to request data or more complex logic.
28: 
29: Proxy is _not_ intended for slow data fetching. While Proxy can be helpful for [optimistic checks](/docs/app/guides/authentication#optimistic-checks-with-proxy-optional) such as permission-based redirects, it should not be used as a full session management or authorization solution.
30: 
31: Using fetch with `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, or `options.next.tags`, has no effect in Proxy.
32: 
33: ### Convention
34: 
35: Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.
36: 
37: > **Note**: While only one `proxy.ts` file is supported per project, you can still organize your proxy logic into modules. Break out proxy functionalities into separate `.ts` or `.js` files and import them into your main `proxy.ts` file. This allows for cleaner management of route-specific proxy, aggregated in the `proxy.ts` for centralized control. By enforcing a single proxy file, it simplifies configuration, prevents potential conflicts, and optimizes performance by avoiding multiple proxy layers.
38: 
39: ### Example
40: 
41: You can export your proxy function as either a default export or a named `proxy` export:
42: 
43: ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
44: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
45: import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
46: 
47: // This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
48: export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
49:   return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
50: }
51: 
52: // Alternatively, you can use a default export:
53: // export default function proxy(request: NextRequest) { ... }
54: 
55: export const config = {
56:   matcher: '/about/:path*',
57: }
58: ```
59: 
60: ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
61: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
62: 
63: // This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
64: export function proxy(request) {
65:   return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
66: }
67: 
68: // Alternatively, you can use a default export:
69: // export default function proxy(request) { ... }
70: 
71: export const config = {
72:   matcher: '/about/:path*',
73: }
74: ```
75: 
76: The `matcher` config allows you to filter Proxy to run on specific paths. See the [Matcher](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#matcher) documentation for more details on path matching.
77: 
78: Read more about [using `proxy`](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#proxy), or refer to the `proxy` [API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

# @aevryn/auth

Framework-agnostic Supabase auth helpers (replaces the legacy better-auth setup).

## Exports

| Subpath | Contents |
|---|---|
| `.` | re-exports everything below |
| `./server` | `createServerSupabase(cookies)` SSR client, `createAdminClient()` service-role client, `CookieMethodsServer` type |
| `./client` | `getBrowserSupabase()` browser singleton |
| `./user` | `getCurrentUser(supabase)`, `requireUser(supabase)` |

## Usage

Server route:

```ts
import { createServerSupabaseForNext } from "@/lib/supabase-server";
import { requireUser } from "@aevryn/auth";

const supabase = await createServerSupabaseForNext();
const user = await requireUser(supabase);
```

Browser component:

```ts
import { supabaseClient } from "@/lib/supabase-client";
const { data } = await supabaseClient.auth.getUser();
```

## Rules

- `createAdminClient()` bypasses RLS — server-only (Storage uploads, triggers).
- Always create a fresh server client per request — never share across requests.
- Token refresh writes land in the proxy (`src/proxy.ts`).

## Objective
- Finish the Aevryn backend/DB rewrite on branch `backend/rewrite` (supabase-backed, 17-table schema). P1 auth (commit `f49a7ca auth(init)` + `ce5e7f5 auth(login)`) is committed; currently fixing a live redirect loop caused by an RLS policy infinite recursion. After the fix: commit 6 `refactor(api)` (tRPC god router → REST services), then services/inngest/chat/queue/ui commits, then the deferred broken-import sweep.

## Important Details
- User directive: overwrite legacy backend files when required (tRPC god router, old schema, old Inngest, old prompts, mocked UI disposable). Broken imports repo-wide = DEFERRED (final pass).
- Supabase CLI NOT installed — user pastes SQL into Supabase dashboard. Glue-style SQL in `packages/db/supabase/migrations/` is the delivery path.
- **Route shape decision (user-approved)**: nested `/workspace/[workspaceId]/[threadId]`. Default workspace resolver at `/workspace` → `/workspace/{wpId}`. Docs updated in ARCHITECTURE/UI/PLAN/AUDIT; **`final-docs/` is gitignored** (doc edits not committed).
- Next 16.3: typed routes via `.next/types`; `bunx next typegen` regenerates them (fixed `RouteImpl<"/onboarding">` error). `redirect()` must target an existing route.
- Web `tsc` baseline: ~100 pre-existing errors (packages/api, packages/inngest, packages/ui, stale `.next` type validators) — expected, deferred; touched files verify clean.
- RLS policies ARE applied in DB (onboarding update worked → user_profiles policies live). Root cause of loop = policy self-reference, not missing policies.
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` now set by user (they added env vars + configured Google OAuth); env validation passes, login/callback/onboarding all work.
- Service-role key used only by `createAdminClient()` (Storage/trigger ops — P10). Not urgent beyond env validation.
- Dead better-auth file: `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` deleted; stale LSP error referencing it is a false positive (file removed).

## Work State
### Completed
- Commits: `f49a7ca auth(init)` (env vars, `packages/auth` supabase rewrite, `proxy.ts`, `/auth/callback`, evlog-auth) and `ce5e7f5 auth(login)` (root+/login `LoginScreen`, `/onboarding` wizard, `POST /api/onboarding`, `/workspace` default resolver, nested routes, `page.old.tsx` preservation).
- P1 auth+onboarding flow: Google login → callback → onboarding questions → saved → `/workspace`. DB rows confirmed via service-role script: 1 user (`2b034975-eb88-448a-a59f-62c80f4e99b9`), workspace `wp_7bec9156239f4cf7b602782a10aff0dd` (Personal, is_default=true), profile `prf_df254bdd47324e0d9fedfe077abf9a6b` (onboarded=true, pre_answers set), 4 system groups, owner membership `wme_7d6ea26321f8494291cb9fe20ee13273`.

- Auto-detected loop symptom; verified DB state good; identified failure leg via debug logs user pasted.

### Active
- Debugging RLS recursion. User-pasted server logs prove both legs:
  - `[onboarding] ... profile: {"onboarded":true,"preAnswers":true}` → redirects to `/workspace`
  - `[workspace-root] ... data: null error: infinite recursion detected in policy for relation "workspace_members"` → redirects to `/onboarding` ⇒ loop.
- Root cause: `workspace_members_select` policy self-subqueries `workspace_members` (0002 migration) → Postgres infinite-recursion error → workspaces select silently null.
- Same bug class suspected in: `workspace_members_insert/update/delete` (self-subquery), `threads_select`/`threads_update` (`exists(select 1 from threads t where t.id = threads.id ...)`), `plans_select/insert/update` (`exists(select 1 from plans p join workflows w ...)` — also suspicious `p.id = plans.workflow_id` comparison). Known-good recency checks like `workspaces_select`/`groups_*` (reference only other tables) are fine.

- JWT-mint RLS test attempt failed (Supabase now RS256, service-role key not the JWT secret) — abandoned; debug logging was the path.

### Blocked

- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` resolved (was blocked). No other blockers.

- `final-docs/plan/PLAN.md`: authoritative roadmap — next is P3 commit 6 `refactor(api)`.

## 2. `final-docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (255 lines)

```
# ARCHITECTURE — Full New Backend + Frontend Logic

Replaces the old tRPC + regex-decision + god-class backend. The system becomes:

```
Browser (Next.js client, zustand stores)
   │  useChat (Vercel AI SDK @ai-sdk/react 4.x)
   ▼
/workspace/[workspaceId]/[threadId]   (client page, no full reload on swap; workspaceId selects context/sidebar)
   │
   ▼  POST /api/chat (ChatTransport → streamText)
   │
   ├── live (fast) tools: askUserQuestion, showPlan, editPlan, memory tools,
   │                      HTTP request tool, media tools (image/transcription live)
   │
   └── durable (Anakin/Inngest) tools: delegateAgenticWork (one tool)
               │
               ▼  inngest.send("thread/run")
               ▼  Inngest fn "thread-runner" streams run_activities rows
               ▼  Supabase Realtime → ChatMessage updates live in place
```

## A. Auth (Supabase, Google only, MVP)

- Root `page.tsx` = login screen. `supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:"google"})`.
- `onLinkIdentity`/redirect to `/workspace` after signup (resolves the
  user's `is_default` workspace → `/workspace/[workspaceId]`).
- Post-signup flow: pre-questions driven by a JSON config (role/usecase/goal,
  multi+single select; user edits the JSON, app maps it to QuestionFlow). Answers
  → `user_profiles.pre_answers`. If signup exists but profile row missing → auto
  navigate to onboarding (create on demand).
- `useSupabaseUser()` hook (zustand + Supabase client). Middleware/proxy
  (`src/proxy.ts` evlog) still runs; tRPC session shim removed — server routes
  read `createServerClient` session from cookies.
- Sessions: Supabase handles refresh (`@supabase/ssr` cookie-based). Server
  side: `createServerClient` with anon/publishable; protected route checks user.

## B. Realtime plumbing

- **Supabase Realtime** on tables: `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` (private channels, JWT-auth user filters).
- Client hooks: `useChatRealtime(threadId)` merges live broadcast rows into the
  chat store / useChat message list. **This is how Inngest-produced activity
  reaches the UI** (durable work streams to an open chat).
- Room id convention `thread:{threadId}` on Realtime channel.

## C. Chat transport & message appending (the "no new message every tool" rule)

Streaming in web via `POST /api/chat` using `ChatTransport` protocol:
- Drive `messages` from DB via `chat_messages`, feed to `streamText`.
- **Live LLM path**: `streamText({model, messages, tools, toolApproval,
  stopWhen: isStepCount(maxSteps), system: composeSystem(workflow, plan, memory)})`
  → `toUIMessageStream` → `createUIMessageStreamResponse`. Returns typed
  `UIMessage` parts; `useChat`/`Chat` client keeps ONE assistant message alive
  and appends tool parts to it.
- **Durable path**: when a tool needs Inngest (Anakin, browser, sleep/schedule),
  the route/handler calls `inngest.send("thread/run", ...)` and returns a
  "delegated" tool part with the `run_id`; UI shows ThinkingSteps derived from
  `run_activities` streamed in. When the run completes, the ChatMessage gets a
  final assistant part (result text). No new message bubbles for sub-steps —
  everything appends to the same assistant message.
- **New ChatMessage(assistant) triggers** ONLY: error, warning, workflow stops
  unexpectedly, user stops → user clicks Run again. (Per user rule.)

```tsx
// client pseudocode — the appending contract
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult, stop } = useChat({ api: "/api/chat", id: threadId });
// useChat actually uses Chat/DefaultChatTransport — bridge in provider
```

## D. Tool surface (LLM-invocable, zod schemas, NEVER hardcoded)

| Tool | When | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `askQuestion` | clarifying questions (any time LLM needs) | live — returns `AskUserQuestion[]` JSON → UI renders ask-user-questions (MCQ) |
| `showPlan` | ONLY when user explicitly asks to plan/workflow (NO auto-plan) | live — returns `{steps: [...], header}` → AccordionGroup |
| `editPlan` | add/remove/update any step | live — persists `plan_steps` |
| `finalizeAndInject` | user approves → bind thread↔workflow, set status | live + sends thread/run if "run" chosen |
| `bindWorkflow` (variant) | approve-but-not-run | live — bind only, workflow idle; Run button appears, Stop hidden. Run toggles→Stop while running |
| `storeMemory` / `searchMemory` | thread + global memory (mem0) | live (mem0 low-latency); ONE mem0 store per user, thread scoped by metadata |
| `httpRequest` | user bearer token, arbitrary HTTP | live — raw fetch; https-only, private-IP blocked, size/max-redirect caps |
| `delegateAgenticWork` | ANY Anakin capability (search/scrape/crawl/map/research/wire/browser + schedule) | durable → Inngest `thread/run`; returns run_id |
| `generateImage` / `transcribeAudio` | media generation requests | live when `IMAGE_MODEL`/`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` set per workspace/env |

- `askQuestion` → `AskUserQuestion` schema (packages/ui
  `ask-user-questions.tsx:37`) — single zod schema shared server+client.
- Auto-approve switch: toolApproval config + `approval_requests` row status
  auto-"approved" when workflow.auto_approve; system message emitted
  "auto-approved via settings".
- **NO auto-plan/wiring**: LLM answers plain text, never auto-creates a plan or
  binds a workflow on its own. `showPlan` only fires after user explicitly asks
  ("create a workflow / plan this"). A 2nd user message is NOT a plan trigger.
- **Attachments → LLM-readable**: image/pdf/video dropped into ChatComposer get
  converted to LLM input parts (image → data URL / base64 image part; pdf →
  extracted text part) before the call; media tools return real content.

## E. Durable execution (Inngest): `thread/run`

- ONE event: `thread/run` (down from pile). `thread-runner` function:
  1. fetch everything from DB (thread, plan, memory summaries, previous runs).
  2. `generateText`/`ToolLoopAgent` with the SAME tool set minus the durable
     re-delegation (no recursion);
  3. persist each step/tool into `runs` + `run_activities` + broadcast.
  4. sleep/resume via `runs.status=sleeping` + schedule-tick (FIXED: add proper
     Inngest `triggers: [{ event:... }]` or `cron`) — and register ALL functions
     in `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts` serve list.
  5. notify on completion/failure → `notifications`.
- Idempotency: `runs.status` gate `pending→running` with `select ... for update`
  in Postgres; retries honor existing activity instead of re-running.
- Cost caps: check BEFORE each step (realtime), not after the run (fix the
  old post-hoc bug).

## F. Frontend state (zustand)

- Zustand stores (each `[thread]`, `[sidebar]`, `[chatComposer]`, `[ui/theme]`,
  `[auth]`) — keeps server components pure; zustand used max; no useState sprawl.
- `threadId` navigation: `router.push('/workspace/'+workspaceId+'/'+id, { scroll:false })` — both segments carried; a thread is always viewed from the context workspace (own PERSONAL or a joined workspace).
  updating only param; page reads `params.threadId` once → store. ChatComposer
  layout: centered when no messages → bottom once first message exists.
- ChatComposer: queue (ordered, editable, removable, durable-backend),
  token-quality slider formula: `maxTokens per CHAT request` (this is what the
  slider means; maps to `streamText.maxOutputTokens`, not a run budget),
  file/image/pdf attach → compress (canvas, WebP, quality 0.8, max 2000px) →
  Supabase Storage → `files` row + `UIMessage` attachments.
- Queue `chat_messages.status=queued`: on run finish, drain SEQUENTIALLY —
  deliver message, wait for that response to finish, then next (no parallel
  queue burst). Edited/reordered queue → DB rows updated in place, order kept.

## G. Memory (mem0, ONE place per user, thread-scoped)

- ONE mem0 store per app user (as chosen): every thread's memories live there,
  scoped by `metadata.threadId`. `storeMemory`/`searchMemory` tools:
  - thread scope: `{scope:"thread", threadId}` — memories only reprompted for
    that thread.
  - global scope: `{scope:"global"}` — **program-given memory injected
    beforehand**, works across ALL workspaces/threads/apps for that user (not
    per-workspace). E.g. capability schemas, user prefs, standing instructions.
- `packages/agent/src/adapters/README.md:1` resolution: adapter schemas exposed
  to LLM via GLOBAL memory (per decision) — one tool `listCapabilities` returns
  schemas; keeps them OO-reflectable.

## I. Permission model — invites, roles, sharing (locked answers)

### Role set (ONE model everywhere)
`owner | editor | viewer` — **no admin**. | Action | owner | editor | viewer | thread-guest |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| rename / delete workspace, keys, settings | yes | — | — | — |
| manage members (invite/role/remove) | yes | — | — | — |
| create / rename / delete groups & threads | yes | yes | — | — |
| edit plans, bind workflows | yes | yes | — | — |
| send msgs, run/stop, approve approvals | yes | yes | — | yes |
| view history / runs / plan | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| rename / rebind / re-share / delete shared thread | yes | — | — | — |

> thread-guest = the person invited to a SPECIFIC thread (thread share). Editor
> = member of the shared workspace.

### Workspace invite (join the REAL workspace)
1. Owner (only) copies workspace invite link / shares by email → `invites` row
   (`kind=workspace`, role editor|viewer chosen at invite).
2. Invitee accepts → `workspace_members` row (role as invited). NO copy, no new
   workspace — it's the owner's actual workspace. Workspace appears in the
   invitee's top-left switcher (badge on the button) → switching in shows ALL
   groups + threads (all members see everything).
3. Members chat/run using the **workspace's keys** (owner pays) UNLESS profile
   toggle "use my own keys in invited workspaces" is on → member's own
   workspace keys are used. `get_workspace_key` RPC + key-service honor this.
4. Owner can change roles / remove / revoke anytime. Editor can delete any
   thread/group (even others'). Viewer read-only.

### Thread share (guest in YOUR sidebar)
1. Owner toggles `threads.share_enabled` and copies the thread share link
   (per-thread; the "list of my threads + switch" UI in Members/Share).
2. Invitee accepts → `thread_shares` row. The LIVE SAME thread (not a copy)
   appears in the invitee's OWN workspace sidebar under the **INVITES system
   group** (created locked+empty at signup; only fills via accepted invites),
   with a Badge on the thread button and on the header. Both users
   chat in the same realtime thread.
3. Invitee's messages use **their own keys**; their name shows on user bubbles.
4. Owner revokes by flipping share_enabled / deleting the share.

### Keys resolution order (chat / run)
```
1. member in a shared workspace + prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
      → member's OWN Personal workspace keys (type: groq|anakin|mem0|…)
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env defaults (ANAKIN_API_KEY / GROQ_API_KEY / MEM0_API_KEY / models)
```

## J. Packages map (rewrite targets)

| Package | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `@aevryn/auth` | better-auth | Supabase client + SSR + google + onboarding trigger |
| `@aevryn/api` | tRPC router | dropped for chat (chat = `POST /api/chat`); keep minimal health/metadata route if needed |
| `@aevryn/agent` | runtime + registry + regex | `runAgent` live (streamText), durable `thread-runner`, tools from schema library |
| `@aevryn/workflow` | god service 66 methods | split: thread-service, plan-service, run-service, activity-service, notification-service, key-service, **member-service** (invites, roles, shares) |
| `@aevryn/inngest` | 3 functions, 1 served | serve ALL fns; `thread-runner` + `schedule-tick` (Inngest cron) + notify |
| `@aevryn/db` | 16 tables legacy | new SCHEMA.md (17 tables) + Supabase migration |
| `@aevryn/env` | server only | server + web split, USER keys via DB Vault (see ENV.md) |
| `@aevryn/ui` | components (keep) | real-data wiring (dropdown, nav, dialogs), ChatMessage attachments, ProfileDialog, Toaster mount |

## K. Flow verification scenarios (must "just work")

1. **"Hi"** → user text only, LLM plain text, NO tool call, NO new workflow.
2. **"plan me a laptop comparison"** → LLM askQuestion (MCQ) → user answers →
   showPlan accordion → workflowApproval (approve/decline/bind/run) → bind →
   `thread/run` → ThinkingSteps stream research/scrape sub-tasks into the SAME
   assistant message → final answer text appended.
3. **"scrape X.com profile" (no plan)** → delegateAgenticWork → durable run →
   run_activities stream → final text in same message.
4. **user closes tab mid-run** → run continues in Inngest; reopening
   workspace reloads `chat_messages` + `run_activities` → renders state.
5. **queued "delete workflow" while run active** → message queued durable;
   once run completes → queued delivered SEQUENTIALLY (wait each).
6. **auto-approve ON** → approval resolves instantly + system message.
7. **workspace invite** → invitee opens link, accepts → workspace in switcher
   (badge), ALL threads visible, chats charge workspace keys (owner) unless
   invitee's "use my own keys" toggle → own keys.
8. **thread share** → owner toggles share, guest accepts → SAME live thread in
   guest's INVITES group + header badge, guest chats with OWN keys + name on
   bubbles, cannot edit plan/rename; owner revoke removes access instantly.
9. **deleted thread** → soft-archive 30 days (trash), recover → live;
   after 30 days hard-delete (incl. runs/activities/files).
10. **"re-run last run"** → play a rerun (trigger=rerun) with same plan, no
    new chat; hits new `runs` row, streams activities again.
11. **first message** → auto-titles thread; title editable after.

## L. Non-goals / pinned decisions
- Markdown rendering: FUTURE (write API to be parser-friendly — parts, no
  prose-heavy gating). Output contract ready for it.
- Media generation: IMAGE + TRANSCRIPTION SHIPPED in MVP (lazy-load provider
  when `IMAGE_MODEL`/`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` configured); SPEECH/VIDEO stay schemas
  only until models exist. Attachments always converted to LLM-readable parts.
- Sub-agents in parallel: FUTURE phase (see FEATURES.md); design tool outputs as
  containers so sub-agent results merge into `run_activities`.
- Creating MULTIPLE owned workspaces: FUTURE (pro tier). MVP = 1 owned
  Personal + unlimited JOINED workspaces (via invite).
- Shared-thread plan editing by guests: OFF (owner/editor only).

## Product features (locked in docs; see NOTES "Decisions" & PLAN.md)
1. **Soft-archive delete**: deleting a thread/workflow sets `threads.deleted_at`;
   recoverable 30 days (trash), then hard-delete incl. Storage. Never silent.
2. **Smart auto-title**: thread title automatically set from the first user
   message (truncated); rename still available. No blank "New thread".
3. **One Run mental model**: Run button AND the LLM both fire `thread/run`
   (same event). WorkflowApproval dialog = max 4 buttons: Approve+Run /
   Approve / Decline / Edit plan. No dead dropdowns.
4. **Model presets**: Agent/Env tab shows a per-provider list of known model
   ids (searchable) + free-text override; picks write `workspace_api_keys.model_name`.
5. **Share preview page**: share link lands on a preview (thread title + owner
   name only, NO content) with Accept — content stays private until accepted.
6. **Export/import thread**: single JSON (plan + steps + key messages,
   keys stripped) for export/import — template/reuse path.
7. **Re-run**: from a past Run play a rerun with the same plan, no new chat
   (`runs.rerun_of`, trigger=rerun).

## 3. Confirmed breakages (behind "cron not working", "AI SDK not working")

1. **`schedule-tick` has no trigger and is never served.**
   `packages/inngest/src/functions/schedule-tick.ts:21-25` declares
   `inngest.createFunction({ id: "schedule-tick", retries: 2 }, ...)` with no
   `triggers` array, and `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts:9` registers
   ONLY `executionRun`. Result: cron jobs, sleep→wake, and due-work sweeping
   can never fire. This is the root cause of "cron broken".

2. **`notificationNotifier` is also never served.** `notification/publish`
   events (`execution-run.ts:763`) are dropped at the SDK boundary → webhook
   notifications and anywhere-outside-the-app delivery are dead.

3. **`resumeWorkflow` does nothing useful.**
   `workflow-service.ts:1024` flips `paused → active` but never enqueues a new
   execution or sends `execution/run`. A "resumed" workflow sits idle forever.

4. **Orphaned executions on event-send failure.** Every mutator in
   `agent.ts` (`sendMessage`, `confirmWorkflow`, `updateObjective`,
   `runWorkflow`, `resolveApproval`) follows
   `enqueueMessage() → inngest.send()` and on send error calls
   `failExecution()`, but the row created by `enqueueMessage` stays
   `pending`. If `inngest.send` throws after enqueue, nothing ever processes
   that execution → permanent orphan. This send+fail block is copy-pasted 5×
   and is the prime candidate to kill when `/api/chat` takes over.

5. **Decision parsing is regex over free-text.** `extractPlan`/`extractDecision`
   (`execution-run.ts:48`) parse a fenced ```json block out of the model's
   final message. Fragile by design and contradicts AGENTS.md rule 8/9/10
   (structured schemas, no free-text control). The re-architecture replaces it
   with real SDK tool calls. Same for `planning.ts:21` (JSON-in-prose).

6. **Cost budget is post-hoc, not bound.** `runAgentStep` checks
   `result.usage.costUsd > EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` AFTER the whole run completes
   (`execution-run.ts:594`). It can never stop a run from overspending, it only
   schedules a recovery afterwards.

7. **`replayedToolOutputs` is keyed by tool name** (`runtime.ts:160`) and
   consumed once. Fine for the single-retry case, but two capabilities with the
   same name would collide; also replay happens before the response cap, so a
   huge persisted output can refill context.

8. **`GROQ_MODEL` default is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`** (`packages/env/src/server.ts:35`).
   Verify this exact model id exists on Groq — if the dev was running a local

Resolution order at call time:
```
1. member of a SHARED workspace + user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared=true
     → member's OWN Personal workspace keys
2. workspace keys (the workspace the thread belongs to)
3. env default

- **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
  dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
  CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).

    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner

    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.

  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.

- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
  until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
  ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
- `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
  accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
- `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
  run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
  `threads.user_id`).
- `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
  replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
- `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
  directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
  killing the god-table smell.
- `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
  by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
- Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
  → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

<skill_content name="writing-plans">
# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

	async createWorkflow(input: CreateWorkflow): Promise<CreateWorkflowOutcome> {
		const parsed = createWorkflowSchema.parse(input);
		return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
			const workflow = await this.workflows.insert(
				{
					userId: parsed.userId,
					objective: parsed.objective,
				},
				tx,
			);
			await this.events.insert(
				{
					workflowId: workflow.id,
					type: "workflow.created",
					data: {},
				},
				tx,
			);
			return { workflow };
		});
	}

	async startExecution(input: StartExecution): Promise<StartExecutionOutcome> {
		const parsed = startExecutionSchema.parse(input);
		return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
			const workflow = await this.workflows.requireById(parsed.workflowId, tx);
			const execution = await this.executions.insert(
				{
					workflowId: workflow.id,
					status: "running",
					startedAt: new Date(),
					prompt: parsed.prompt ?? "",
				},
				tx,
			);
			await this.workflows.setStatus(workflow.id, "active", tx);
			await this.events.insert(
				{
					workflowId: workflow.id,
					executionId: execution.id,
					type: "execution.started",
					data: {},
				},
				tx,
			);
			return { workflow, execution };
		});
	}

	async getWorkflowById(workflowId: string): Promise<Workflow | null> {
		return this.workflows.findById(workflowId);
	}

	/**
	 * Record a durable recovery attempt. Idempotent per (execution, attempt):
	 * re-runs of a failed function must not duplicate rows.
	 */
	async recordRecoveryAttempt(
		input: CreateRecoveryAttempt,
	): Promise<RecoveryAttempt | null> {
		const parsed = createRecoveryAttemptSchema.parse(input);
		const exists = await this.recoveries.existsByExecutionAttempt(
			parsed.executionId,
			parsed.attempt,
		);
		if (exists) {
			return null;
		}
		const attempt = await this.recoveries.insert({
			workflowId: parsed.workflowId,
			executionId: parsed.executionId,
			stepId: parsed.stepId,
			failureClass: parsed.failureClass,
			failureCode: parsed.failureCode,
			attempt: parsed.attempt,
			strategy: parsed.strategy,
			result: parsed.result,
			detail: parsed.detail,
		});
		await this.events.insert({
			workflowId: parsed.workflowId,
			executionId: parsed.executionId,
			type: "recovery.started",
			data: {
				attempt: attempt.attempt,
				failureClass: attempt.failureClass,
				failureCode: attempt.failureCode ?? null,
			},
		});
		return attempt;
	}

	async countRecoveryAttempts(executionId: string): Promise<number> {

	/**
	 * Append a user message to a thread as a new durable execution. The
	 * workflow's own status is untouched: a draft stays draft while the
	 * message is planned, an active workflow stays active while it runs.
	 */
	async enqueueMessage(
		workflowId: string,
		prompt: string,
	): Promise<StartExecutionOutcome> {
		return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
			const workflow = await this.workflows.requireById(workflowId, tx);
			const execution = await this.executions.insert(
				{
					workflowId: workflow.id,
					status: "running",
					startedAt: new Date(),
					prompt,
				},
				tx,
			);
			await this.events.insert(
				{
					workflowId: workflow.id,
					executionId: execution.id,
					type: "execution.started",
					data: {},
				},
				tx,
			);
			return { workflow, execution };
		});
	}

	async recordSteps(input: RecordSteps): Promise<RecordStepsOutcome> {
		const parsed = recordStepsSchema.parse(input);
		const execution = await this.executions.requireById(parsed.executionId);
		return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
			const stepRows = await this.steps.insertMany(
				parsed.steps.map((step) => ({
					executionId: execution.id,
					kind: step.kind,
					assistantText: step.text ?? null,
					status: step.toolCalls.every((call) => call.status === "completed")
						? "completed"
						: "failed",
					order: step.order,
					startedAt: step.createdAt,
					completedAt: step.createdAt,
				})),
				tx,
			);
			const stepById = new Map(stepRows.map((row) => [row.order, row]));
			let toolOrder = 0;
			const toolRows = [];
			for (const step of parsed.steps) {
				const stepRow = stepById.get(step.order);
				for (const call of step.toolCalls) {
					toolRows.push(
						this.toToolExecutionRow(
							execution.workflowId,
							execution.id,
							stepRow?.id ?? null,
							toolOrder++,
							call,
						),
					);
				}
			}
			if (toolRows.length > 0) {
				await this.toolExecutions.upsertManyByOrder(toolRows, tx);
			}
			return {
				stepCount: stepRows.length,
				toolCallCount: toolRows.length,
			};
		});
	}

	async completeExecution(input: CompleteExecution): Promise<void> {
		const parsed = completeExecutionSchema.parse(input);
		return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
			const execution = await this.executions.update(
				parsed.executionId,
				{ status: "completed", completedAt: new Date() },
				tx,
			);
			const workflow = await this.workflows.findById(execution.workflowId);
			if (workflow && workflow.status !== "draft") {
				await this.workflows.setStatus(execution.workflowId, "completed", tx);
			}
			await this.events.insert(
				{
					workflowId: execution.workflowId,
					executionId: execution.id,
					type: "execution.completed",
					data: {},
				},
				tx,
			);
		});
	}

			if (workflow && workflow.status !== "draft") {

			}
			await this.events.insert(
				{
					workflowId: execution.workflowId,

		});
	}

	async applyState(input: ApplyState): Promise<{ version: number }> {
		const parsed = applyStateSchema.parse(input);
		const existing = await this.states.findByWorkflow(parsed.workflowId);
		if (!existing) {
			const next = this.mergeState({}, parsed.patch);
			await this.states.insert(
				{
					workflowId: parsed.workflowId,
					phase: next.phase,
					data: next,
				},
				db,
			);
			return { version: 1 };
		}
		const next = this.mergeState(existing.data, parsed.patch);
		const updated = await this.states.updateIfVersion(
			parsed.workflowId,
			parsed.expectedVersion,
			{ phase: next.phase, data: next },
			db,
		);
		return { version: updated.version };
	}

	async getState(workflowId: string): Promise<AgentStateValue | null> {
		const state = await this.states.findByWorkflow(workflowId);
		return state?.data ?? null;
	}

	/**
	 * Persist a live activity snapshot for a workflow. Overwrites the previous
	 * snapshot, so repeated writes are idempotent and safe across retries.
	 */
	async updateActivitySnapshot(
		workflowId: string,
		snapshot: ActivitySnapshot,
	): Promise<void> {
		const parsed = activitySnapshotSchema.parse(snapshot);
		const existing = await this.states.findByWorkflow(workflowId);
		await this.states.upsert(workflowId, {
			phase: "executing",
			data: {
				...existing?.data,
				data: {
					...(existing?.data?.data ?? {}),
					activity: parsed,
				},
			},
		});
	}

	async getActivitySnapshot(
		workflowId: string,
	): Promise<ActivitySnapshot | null> {
		const state = await this.states.findByWorkflow(workflowId);
		const activity = state?.data?.data?.activity;
		if (!activity) {
			return null;
		}
		const parsed = activitySnapshotSchema.safeParse(activity);
		return parsed.success ? parsed.data : null;
	}

	async getExecutionTimeline(executionId: string): Promise<{
		workflow: Workflow;
		execution: WorkflowExecution;
		steps: WorkflowStep[];
		toolExecutions: ToolExecution[];
		activity: ActivitySnapshot | null;
	}> {
		const execution = await this.executions.requireById(executionId);
		const workflow = await this.workflows.requireById(execution.workflowId);
		const activity = await this.getActivitySnapshot(workflow.id);
		return {
			workflow,
			execution,
			steps: await this.steps.listByExecution(execution.id),
			toolExecutions: await this.toolExecutions.listByExecution(execution.id),
			activity,
		};
	}

	async getThread(workflowId: string): Promise<{
		workflow: Workflow;
		plan: Plan | null;
		planProgress: PlanProgress | null;
		activity: ActivitySnapshot | null;
		schedules: Schedule[];
		notifications: Notification[];
		observations: Observation[];
		recoveryAttempts: RecoveryAttempt[];
		approvals: Approval[];
		turns: Array<{
			execution: WorkflowExecution;
			steps: WorkflowStep[];
			toolExecutions: ToolExecution[];
		}>;
	}> {
		const workflow = await this.workflows.requireById(workflowId);
		const executions = await this.executions.listByWorkflowChronological(
			workflowId,
			50,
		);
		const turns = await Promise.all(
			executions.map(async (execution) => ({
				execution,
				steps: await this.steps.listByExecution(execution.id),
				toolExecutions: await this.toolExecutions.listByExecution(execution.id),
			})),
		);
		return {
			workflow,
			plan: await this.getPlan(workflowId),
			planProgress: await this.getPlanProgress(workflowId),
			activity: await this.getActivitySnapshot(workflowId),
			schedules: await this.schedules.listByWorkflow(workflowId),
			notifications: await this.notifications.listByWorkflow(workflowId, 50),
			observations: await this.observations.listByWorkflow(workflowId),
			recoveryAttempts: await this.recoveries.listByWorkflow(workflowId, 20),
			approvals: await this.approvals.listByWorkflow(workflowId, 50),
			turns,
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Assemble the prior conversation in a thread as replay context for the
	 * current run. History is bounded by maxChars (the same context-cap the
	 * user controls). Content is compacted: the MOST RECENT turns are kept,
	 * long answers are trimmed, and the oldest omitted turns are reduced to a
	 * single count line so the model knows history exists without paying its
	 * full token cost.
	 */
	async getConversationContext(
		workflowId: string,
		excludeExecutionId: string,
		maxChars: number | undefined,
	): Promise<string | null> {
		const budget = maxChars ?? 6000;
		const executions = await this.executions.listByWorkflowChronological(
			workflowId,
			50,
		);
		const turns: Array<{ prompt: string; answer: string }> = [];
		for (const execution of executions) {
			if (execution.id === excludeExecutionId || !execution.prompt) {
				continue;
			}
			const steps = await this.steps.listByExecution(execution.id);
			const answer = steps[0]?.assistantText?.trim();
			if (!answer) {
				continue;
			}
			turns.push({
				prompt: execution.prompt,
				answer: answer.length > 1200 ? `${answer.slice(0, 1200)}…` : answer,
			});
		}
		if (turns.length === 0) {
			return null;
		}
		const blocks: string[] = [];
		let used = 0;
		let omitted = 0;
		for (const turn of turns.reverse()) {
			const block = `user: ${turn.prompt}\nassistant: ${turn.answer}`;
			if (used + block.length > budget) {
				omitted += 1;
				continue;
			}
			blocks.push(block);
			used += block.length;
		}
		if (blocks.length === 0) {
			return null;
		}
		const header =
			omitted > 0
				? `Prior messages in this thread (${omitted} older message${omitted === 1 ? "" : "s"} summarized and omitted for space):`
				: "Prior messages in this thread:";
		return `${header}\n${blocks.join("\n\n")}`;
	}

		await this.states.upsert(workflowId, {

				data: {

				},
			},

	}
